fact_text: Interloop is a Pakistani textile maker best known for socks, with global brands such as Nike, Adidas, Puma, Hugo Boss and Uniqlo among its clients.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop was named Pakistan's largest exporter in 2024.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop began in 1992 with 10 knitting machines.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop runs six sock plants, two apparel plants and one denim plant, and operates more than 5,000 knitting machines.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop's sock plants have an annual capacity of about 750 million pairs; five of the six are in Faisalabad and one is in Lahore.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop's two apparel plants in Faisalabad can make about 34 million garment pieces a year, and its Lahore denim plant about 10 million garments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Price-sensitive retailers spend roughly 50-60% of their total cost on buying products and will switch to a cheaper supplier for even a small saving.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Brand-led retailers spend only about 15-30% of their total cost on manufacturing and product buying, putting the rest into marketing, celebrity endorsements, premium stores and rent.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A textile owner told the analyst that price-sensitive retailers change supplier for a 2% saving, change city for 3% and change country for 5%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because product buying is only 15-25% of a brand retailer's cost, a supplier that is 5% dearer adds only about 1% to total cost, so brands weigh quality and delivery above price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Brand retailers require gold-standard certified factories, zero defects, wide colour and design variety, timely delivery and environmental compliance; few suppliers can meet all of them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sees Interloop's long-built relationships with brand retailers as a moat that competitors cannot easily copy, and says this has so far developed only in socks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Most textile companies run at 3-5% net margins, while Interloop has run at double-digit net margins, which the analyst attributes to its brand-retailer relationships rather than to low prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's view the sock business is mature and strong, but unlikely to deliver explosive growth because the global sock market is already mature and Interloop is already large in it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst considers the apparel market many times larger than socks, so a multi-bagger outcome would need Interloop to build a moat in apparel, which it has not yet done.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Denim is a turnaround: early losses from building a new supply chain and discounting to win orders gave way to operating profit, but customer relationships and pricing power are still forming.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects gradual denim improvement in FY27 and FY28, while a moat in denim may take longer to establish.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects the apparel segment to reach break-even or slight profitability by FY27, after its losses narrowed sharply in the second and third quarters of FY26.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst tracks apparel's quarterly operating margin; a move toward 15-20% would signal that a moat is developing in apparel.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An analyst scenario for FY27 puts Interloop's combined revenue at PKR 180-185 billion with a 22-24% gross margin and PKR 27-30 billion operating profit; the analyst says this is illustrative, not a forecast.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's check on the new sock plant assumes about $1 after-tax profit per dozen pairs on a $58 million plant, implying roughly 20% dollar return on capital; this is a scenario, not a result.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The board approved a new $58 million investment in June 2024 for a sock plant producing 12-15 million dozen pairs a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop's Egypt venture is a $35 million ready-made garment plant in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, planned to be operational in 2027.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the Egypt plant should cut shipping time by 20-30 days versus Pakistan for European and US orders, securing delivery for fast-fashion clients and supply-chain reliability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Shipping an order from Pakistan to Europe or the USA typically takes 30-60 days, too slow for fast-fashion retailers that need stock within about four weeks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Nike targets a 30% cut in supply-chain emissions by 2030, and Adidas targets a 30% absolute cut from 2017 levels by 2030; both aim for net zero by 2050.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Brand buyers now include ESG credentials in supplier selection alongside price and quality, which favours suppliers with solar power, biomass boilers and water recycling.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop's production base includes 10 MW of solar, biomass boilers, LEED Platinum certified plants and a 20,000 cubic metre water recycling plant, aligning it with brand ESG requirements.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Budget 2026 cut the minimum tax on exporters from 2% to 1.25%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The prime minister directed that the 10% super tax on exporters be fully eliminated; the analyst notes this was a directive still to be confirmed rather than settled law.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Budget 2026 reduced import duties on some raw materials used by exporters.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Owners of a long-payback project may wait 5-10 years for returns, whereas a minority shareholder can buy once earnings power and value realisation are visible.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst suggests a 3-4 year horizon suits companies where value realisation is likely within a few years, and that entry should wait until earnings power and value realisation are both visible.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Global Brands Pay Premium Prices to Interloop | Pakistan's Hidden Export Giant' (YouTube transcript, undated)
